I brought my 1976 MG Midget to ASM Auto Upholstery along with a carpet kit manufactured by a reputable company in England.

Karen, the daughter of the owner, gave me all kinds of warnings about what could go wrong with the carpet installation. She said they may break the seat bolts. The carpet kit may be cut wrong by the factory. They may have lots of trouble removing the original carpet adhesive and backing.  She couldn’t give me a firm estimate and would charge labor for however many hours it took. After I asked for a rough estimate, the top of her range was $1800. She charged $2100 dollars for 14 hours labor.

I would have no issue with all of this if the end result was good. See my photos of the area behind the driver seat, which, luckily, is not usually visible. It’s as if the installer was rushing toward the end of the installation and thought about how this area was not visible.

Karen’s explanation was that the carpet was inferior and that the threads can be pulled out with a tweezer. I’m not buying this. It’s apparent that the installer had to pull the new carpet loose after gluing it incorrectly. Either the threads pulled through the back of the carpet or the installer just pulled the threads loose in an attempt to loosen the carpet to reposition it. There is a bunched area at the top because the carpet is still not positioned correctly.

An adjacent piece of carpet that covers the transmission tunnel is installed crooked and in a way that it overlaps the piece behind the driver seat. I can’t figure out why the factory cut this panel in such a way, but the way it’s installed is wrong and appears to be an attempt to cover more damage to the piece behind the driver seat.

After paying and driving the car home, I brought these issues to Karen’s attention via email. She called me right away and said the carpet material is cheap and that some of the pieces were either too big or too small. The factory in England says on their website that the pieces are laser cut and will always fit, which may not be true.

It was apparent from the beginning that Karen’s initial warnings were given to ensure the validity of her “I told you so” explanations. I do understand that, with a carpet kit, they have only one chance to get it right since there is no extra carpet.

If they were acting in a way to maintain their reputation, the installer would have stopped working after damaging the carpet. I would have been informed and provided with options. I could have ordered a replacement piece of carpet for a do-over. I would have paid for the additional labor. At this later time, however, the seats would have to be removed again and I’m not sure that adjacent pieces of carpet wouldn’t be damaged during a do-over.

Ultimately, it seems that they accept an inferior result as long as they can blame someone else - the carpet manufacturer or me, for bringing in a carpet kit. They aren’t really interested in doing as good a job as they can. By stopping work to evaluate the bad result, they could have provided me with options.

I can't review the quality of their work, as I was never given a chance to see the final product in the first place. I visited thier website and submitted an inquiry ticket for reupholstering and re-padding a motorcycle seat. Waited a week; no response. My short and simple history:
On October 27, 2025
Ford Escape Hybrid 2011. Transmission stuck in “Parking”. Towed the car in (paid out of pocket).
They charged $150 for “diagnostics” and then claimed the transmission was bad and needed replacement for $3700.

❗ No estimate. No invoice. No proof of any real inspection.

I later fixed it myself in 15 minutes by checking the transmission linkage — the car drives fine.
This shop looks like a scam.
$150 for nothing.

I paid 6000 to have my transmission replaced. After that my car kept stalling when taking a turn. They tried to charge me even more saying the collision sensor might need to be replaced but wouldn’t take responsibility for them breaking it since the sensor was fine before they replaced the transmission.

Friendly staff and owner. Carefully explained details of repairs. Responds to questions. On the business side, I had difficulties with my repairs. I paid  $5500 to have my transmission rebuilt. I took it back on 3x after I received it back because it still wasn’t running back. On the third time, I was told it was another part not covered under my transmission warranty causing the problem. I paid more money. Drove away and 14 months later ( 2 months after my warranty) the transmission overheated and needed to completely rebuilt again!  Hell NO! I changed this from a one to three star because the owner called me personally with genuine concern how to resolve the issue.  I gave up and bought new vehicle. I’m done.

They replaced my transmission in October 2023 and I had to return my car to them many times after. My transmission is back having issues and its been one and a half years since they "rebuilt" my transmission. I took it back and they wanted to tell me it might be another $5k to fix my transmission, given that I had already made $5K in the initial repair in 2023. They claimed their warranty only covered 20,000 miles. I would say if you're going to work with these dudes, keep every receipt and get everything in writing. If your repair doesnt go smoothly, you want to HAVE all your ducks in a row. The receptionist CJ also treated my BIL horrible on the phone. He was so rude. The "good customer service" is a facade and I personally dont think their work is consistently good.

Charged me $700 for a water pump replacement. I left my car on Friday morning and got it back on Monday afternoon. As soon as I start to drive I notice a loud screeching sound in my steering system that wasn't there before bringing it in. I go back to the shop and they find my power steering hose has a large hole and is leaking air. The mechanic admits to bending it while working in that area and accidentally causing it to tear. They cut the hose where it's leaking and put it back in its place telling me the noise will go away, Although they don't bother to bleed the air completely out of the power steering system. They tell me to drive for a couple of days but the grinding noise is still there. Again I bring it to the shop and the owner offers to replace the Power Steering Pump without charge if it solves the issue. I go back to the shop later on thinking it was finally fixed only for the owner to say it's not the Power Steering Pump and that I have to pay $120 if I want them to look deeper into the issue.
At this point I take my car back after they've stopped taking accountability for the damage done in their hands...
Turns out it Was the Power Steering Pump. It got damaged after they let air into the system and gave me my car back with a damaged hose. The exact same thing the owner said he'd change but later took back caused me to spend another $500 getting it replaced. Poor customer service and no accountability. You don't expect to spend your hard earned money on one thing just to leave with another issue that wasn't there before. I Rather take my chances anywhere else than to risk something like this happening again.

Unfortunately, I cannot say I had a good experience here. I took my truck in for problems with the transmission slipping and getting error messages. They rebuilt the transmission, but about a week later it was doing the same thing. I took it back in and they did the job again. A few weeks later, I was back and they told me it was a bad sensor and charged me another $350 on top of the over $2500 I had already paid. A few weeks later they changed out the torque converter and I still had the same problem. I put some temperature sensors on it and showed them that it was overheating, but they disagreed with me,  saying that temperatures in the 270' range were fine. Finally, after almost 9 months of going back and forth, I figured out it was a small thermostat outside of the transmission. I took it back and told them about it. They said they checked it and it was fine. I replaced the thermostat myself and my transmission has been fine ever since. The short of it is, While they did make a significant effort, close to $3000 on my part and almost as much on them in labor was spent over a $30 part.

$1,240 for labor by replacing 2 ring bushings inside the transmission the parts weren't even new he used them from and old transmission he had in his shop yet i paid like if they were new. it made no difference my transmission is still leaking. So i went back again on the next day and he said to keep running it 🤨 to me it made no sense, worst thing is that it was only 30" day of warranty OMG,  It's been 2 weeks from then so now i decided to take it somewhere else where they can fix it all the way.
FYI he recommended to buy a used transmission maybe because he didn't wanted to break all apart and see what was the problem. 🤦🏻‍♂️

Price was more than double all competitors. When asked why no reasons could be given. Extremely rude. Because I asked why the price would be more than double I was told I was giving the mechanic a hard time and he told me has decided to not help me. My car has been here 3 times I’m in 6 months.
1. Brought vehicle in for valve cover gasket replacements. They told me that my camshaft position sensor was leaking oil and that would be replaced as well.

Got the car back. Plastic fan shroud was broken. Definitely was not broken when the car was dropped off. Their response was “we did not do that.

2. A couple weeks later, I noticed oil leaking again. It was coming from the camshaft position sensor. The one they told me was going to be replaced.

Brought it back. Since it was not listed on my receipt, I had to pay for the CPS to be replaced. And they also redid the gaskets because they were also leaking in the corners (just replaced)

3. Fast forward about two months . Check engine light has been on and off every couple start ups. Code checks out for vacuum seal failure/misfire.

Bring car back to a-1 for oil change. A couple of days later, I find a big oil stain in my driveway. Look under the hood and the oil cap is loose and leaked oil. Started digging around some more I realized the plenum spacer is now cracked and the bolts that hold the upper intake to the engine are not in the right locations and clearly over torqued causeing the plenum spacer to crack (which is the cause of check engine light and terrible idle and misfires)

When confronted, a-1 was unsure of what oil was used and would not offer and reimbursement toward the now needed repairs. They offered to top off the oil and said “I’m sorry”

The owner has not been reachable. Funny, when I called for work to be done he called me himself to give prices. He even left me a voicemail. But now that there is a problem and his employees made a mistake, he’s nowhere to be found.

Please be kind to your vehicle and take to a place that actually cares about you and your car.
